propositions.text: Applicant brought judicial review under s 72 IRPA of Refugee Protection Division decision
propositions.quote: Otto Balaz (the Applicant) has brought an application for judicial review under s 72 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c.27 (the IRPA) of a decision of the Refugee Protection Division the Immigration Refugee Board (the Board).

propositions.text: Board found Applicant neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection
propositions.quote: The Board determined that the Applicant is neither a Convention refugee within the meaning of s 96 of the IRPA, nor a person in need of protection as defined in s 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant brought judicial review of Board decision finding him neither refugee nor person in need of protection, court states.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, the application for judicial review is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses the application for judicial review.

propositions.text: Applicant is 63, Slovak citizen, arrived May 19, 2012 with family; claim severed; alleges persecution due to Roma ethnicity
propositions.quote: The Applicant is 63 years old and a citizen of Slovakia. He arrived in Canada on May 19, 2012 together with four distant family members. Their claims for refugee protection were initially joined, but the Applicant’s claim was later severed from the others. The Applicant says that he faces persecution in Slovakia because of his Roma ethnicity.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is 63, Slovak citizen, arrived with family; claim severed; alleges persecution due to Roma ethnicity, court states.

propositions.text: Questions arose about POE documents, especially amended Personal Information Form after claim severed
propositions.quote: Questions arose regarding the documents the Applicant completed at the port of entry (POE), particularly in relation to the amended Personal Information Form submitted by his counsel after his claim was severed.

propositions.text: Applicant says mother told story initially; he did not add personal details until claim severed
propositions.quote: The Applicant said that because he was travelling with the other claimants, the mother assumed responsibility for telling their story and it did not occur to him to supplement it with details of his own circumstances. It was only after his claim was separated that he realized the need to provide details of the persecution he faced personally.

propositions.text: Initial narrative referred generally to discrimination and one unpaid job incident with beatings
propositions.quote: Thus, the initial narrative provided on behalf of the Applicant referred only generally to discrimination that the Applicant faced when applying for jobs, and one incident in which he was not paid for a job. In the latter incident, the Applicant and two co-workers were beaten when they asked to be paid.

propositions.text: Police took victims to hospital but said no further help would be provided
propositions.quote: Following this, the police took the victims to the hospital, and told them that the police would be of no further help.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes questions about POE documents; Applicant says mother told story initially; initial narrative mentioned discrimination and beatings; police took victims to hospital but refused further help.

propositions.text: Amended narrative described ongoing Roma persecution since 1985 and detailed recent personal incidents
propositions.quote: In his amended narrative, the Applicant spoke broadly of ongoing persecution of Roma in Slovakia since 1985, and in more detail about his personal experience during the two years preceding his claim.

propositions.text: Repeated beating incident with more detail; four additional beatings including kidnapping and extortion threats
propositions.quote: The incident of being beaten by an employer’s “thugs” was repeated but with more detail. Four additional incidents of beatings were recounted, one in which the Applicant was kidnapped and held for two days. He said that “white people” were extorting him under threat of death.

propositions.text: Applicant went to police thrice but they refused to investigate; hospital visits included denial of treatment once
propositions.quote: The Applicant went to the police on three occasions but they refused to investigate. He was taken to the hospital twice, and was denied treatment on one of these occasions.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's amended narrative described ongoing Roma persecution, detailed beatings including kidnapping, police refusal to investigate, and hospital denial of treatment.

propositions.text: Board concerned narrative was in English, unsigned, no translation certificate
propositions.quote: The Board expressed concern regarding the Applicant’s narrative because it was in English, with no certificate of translation, and it was not signed by the Applicant.

propositions.text: Counsel explained narrative recorded with interpreter; Applicant confirmed under oath it was true and complete
propositions.quote: The Applicant’s counsel explained that the narrative was recorded with the assistance of an interpreter, and the Applicant confirmed under oath that it was true, accurate, and complete.

paragraphs.summary: Board concerned narrative was in English, unsigned, no translation; counsel said interpreter used; Applicant confirmed truth under oath.

propositions.text: Applicant testified he sought police help after kidnapping but omitted it from narrative as repetitive
propositions.quote: In his testimony before the Board, the Applicant said that he sought help from the police after he was kidnapped, but he did not include this detail in the amended narrative because he considered it repetitive.

propositions.text: Applicant said house was illegally expropriated by extortion group
propositions.quote: The Applicant added that his house was illegally expropriated by the group that extorted him.

propositions.text: Further inconsistencies existed between amended narrative and testimony, mainly about incident dates
propositions.quote: There were also further inconsistencies between the amended narrative and the Applicant’s testimony before the Board, primarily with respect to the dates on which the incidents occurred.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant testified he sought police help after kidnapping but omitted it; said house expropriated; inconsistencies existed between narrative and testimony on dates.

propositions.text: Board found Applicant neither refugee nor person in need of protection
propositions.quote: In its decision dated November 28, 2013, the Board found that the Applicant was neither a refugee nor a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Board accepted Applicant was beaten
propositions.quote: The Board accepted that the Applicant had been beaten.

propositions.text: Board found many inconsistencies and lack of corroboration, made adverse credibility finding, beatings not persecution
propositions.quote: However, due to the many inconsistencies between the POE documents, his amended narrative and his oral testimony, as well as the lack of corroborating evidence, the Board made an adverse finding of credibility and found that the beatings did not amount to persecution.

propositions.text: Board found Roma face discrimination in Slovakia but presumption of state protection not rebutted
propositions.quote: Based on its analysis of country condition reports, the Board also found that Roma do face discrimination in Slovakia, but the presumption of state protection was not rebutted in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Board found Applicant neither refugee nor protected person; accepted beatings but found inconsistencies and no persecution; Roma face discrimination but state protection presumed.

propositions.text: Issues: reasonableness of Board's findings on credibility, persecution, and state protection
propositions.quote: The following issues are raised by this application for judicial review: A. Whether the Board’s findings with respect to the Applicant’s credibility were reasonable; B. Whether the Board’s finding regarding the Applicant’s lack of persecution was reasonable; and C. Whether the Board’s finding of adequate state protection was reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Court identifies issues: reasonableness of Board's findings on credibility, persecution, and state protection.

propositions.text: All three issues reviewed on reasonableness standard (Dunsmuir)
propositions.quote: All three issues raised in this case are subject to review by this Court against a standard of reasonableness (Dunsmuir v New Brunswick, 2008 SCC 9, [2008] 1 SCR 190).

paragraphs.summary: Court states all issues are reviewed on reasonableness standard per Dunsmuir.

propositions.text: Applicant criticizes Board's paragraphs 24-25 on inconsistency between narrative and testimony about police comments
propositions.quote: The Applicant focuses his criticism on paragraphs 24 and 25 of the Board’s decision, which address an inconsistency between his amended narrative and his oral testimony. The amended narrative states that the police would not help the Applicant and his co-workers, while the Applicant testified at the hearing that the police also told them that they got what they deserved because of their ethnicity.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant criticizes Board's finding on inconsistency between narrative and testimony about police comments.

propositions.text: Small inconsistency alone would not justify adverse credibility finding
propositions.quote: This is admittedly a small inconsistency, and were it the only reason for the Board’s adverse credibility finding then the decision may have been unreasonable.

propositions.text: Board found many inconsistencies cumulatively undermining credibility
propositions.quote: However, a review of the Board’s lengthy and detailed analysis of the Applicant’s credibility confirms that this was only one of many inconsistencies.

propositions.text: Board concluded cumulative effect negated credible evidence for refugee status
propositions.quote: The Board concluded its analysis with the following observation (at para 34): I am aware that none of the concerns raised here may be sufficient, each on its own, to negate the claims. However the cumulative effect of all of them is that I do not have sufficient credible, plausible and trustworthy evidence upon which to base a determination that the claimant is a Convention refugee.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds small inconsistency alone insufficient but Board reasonably found cumulative inconsistencies undermined credibility.

propositions.text: Reasonable for Board to find cumulative inconsistencies undermined credibility, citing cases
propositions.quote: In my view it was reasonable for the Board to find that the cumulative effect of many small inconsistencies undermined the Applicant’s credibility (Cuentas Peralta v Canada (MCI), 2014 FC 962, 245 ACWS (3rd) 410; Karakaya v Canada (MCI), 2014 FC 777, 242 ACWS (3rd) 908; Shah v Canada (MCI), 2013 FC 280, 227 ACRS (3rd) 525).

propositions.text: Board's credibility decision is credible, transparent, and defensible on facts and law
propositions.quote: Read as a whole, the Board’s decision on this point is credible, transparent, and defensible with respect to the facts and law.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Board reasonably concluded cumulative inconsistencies undermined credibility; decision credible and defensible.

propositions.text: Board found discrimination did not reach persecution threshold
propositions.quote: The Board concluded that, although the Applicant faced discrimination in Slovakia, this did not reach the threshold of persecution.

propositions.text: Board found some incidents in narrative were embellished
propositions.quote: The Board also found that some of the incidents described in the amended narrative had been embellished.

paragraphs.summary: Board found discrimination but not persecution; some incidents embellished.

propositions.text: Board found experiences did not rise to persecution level due to negative credibility assessment
propositions.quote: Based on its negative assessment of the Applicant’s credibility, the Board concluded that his experiences of discrimination “do not individually or cumulatively, rise to a level of seriousness of harm amounting to persecution”.

propositions.text: Board's finding on persecution was open to it and court cannot intervene
propositions.quote: This finding of fact that was open to the Board based on the evidence, and there is therefore no basis on which this Court may legitimately intervene.

paragraphs.summary: Board found experiences not persecution due to credibility; court will not intervene on this fact finding.

propositions.text: Application of adequate state protection test is correctness standard; application to facts is reasonableness standard
propositions.quote: In Kina v Canada (MCI), 2014 FC 284, 239 ACWS (3d) 172 at page 24, Justice Russell held that the application of the proper test for adequate state protection is subject to review against the standard of correctness. However, the application of the test to the facts is subject to review against the standard of reasonableness.

propositions.text: Applicant alleges Board's finding on state protection unsupported by evidence, subject to reasonableness review
propositions.quote: Here, it is alleged the Board’s finding was unsupported by the evidence. This falls into the latter category, and attracts a standard of reasonableness.

paragraphs.summary: Court explains state protection test review standards; Applicant alleges Board's finding unsupported, reviewed for reasonableness.

propositions.text: Applicant relies on Cervenakova and Juhasz to argue Board's state protection analysis flawed by focus on efforts not results
propositions.quote: The Applicant relies upon Cervenakova v Canada (MCI), 2012 FC 525, 217 A.C.W.S. (3d) 947 for the proposition that, even if the Board provides a detailed analysis of state protection, this may be undermined by a focus on efforts to improve state protection rather than the results achieved. He also cites my recent decision in Juhasz v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2015 FC 300, 2015.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Board's state protection analysis flawed by focusing on efforts not results, citing cases.

propositions.text: Board found Applicant did not consistently seek state protection
propositions.quote: In this case, the Board reasonably found that the Applicant did not consistently avail himself of state protection.

propositions.text: Board found Applicant admitted not always reporting incidents
propositions.quote: Based on its credibility analysis, together with the Applicant’s admission that he did not always report incidents,

propositions.text: Board found police refused help only once, transported victims to hospital
propositions.quote: the Board concluded that the Applicant was refused help by the police on only one occasion: the incident reported in the initial POE documents. Although the police declined to investigate this incident, they nevertheless provided assistance by transporting the three Roma victims to hospital.

propositions.text: Vagner says Cervenakova focuses on overt police refusal to help, not applicant's efforts
propositions.quote: In Vagner v Canada (MCI), 2014 FC 224, 239 A.C.W.S. (3d) 175, Justice Manson observed that Cervenakova is less concerned with an applicant’s efforts to seek protection than with the overt refusal of the police to help.

paragraphs.summary: Board found Applicant inconsistently sought protection; police refused help once but transported victims; Vagner clarifies focus on police refusal.

propositions.text: Ruszo says RPD misapplication of state protection test not fatal if other grounds support decision
propositions.quote: As Chief Justice Crampton wrote in Ruszo v Canada (MCI), 2013 FC 1004, 2013 CF 1004, [2013] FCJ No 1099: Nevertheless, the RPD’s misunderstanding or misapplication of the “adequate state protection” test is not necessarily fatal in cases where, as here, the RPD also reasonably concluded on other grounds that the Applicants had failed to rebut the presumption of adequate state protection with “clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect [them].”

propositions.text: Failure to show reasonable steps to seek protection and lack of compelling evidence justified RPD decision
propositions.quote: In this case, those grounds were the failure of the Applicants to demonstrate that they had taken all objectively reasonable steps to avail themselves of state protection, and to provide compelling or persuasive evidence to explain their failure to do more than make a single attempt to seek protection from the police.

propositions.text: RPD's alternate basis for decision was important and made decision reasonable
propositions.quote: Having regard to the RPD’s determinations on these points, its decision was not unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Ruszo says RPD misapplication of state protection test not fatal if other grounds support decision; failure to seek protection justified decision.

propositions.text: Mosley says each case decided on facts; Cervenakova involved vague analysis and insufficient basis
propositions.quote: Furthermore, as Justice Mosley held in Minyuova v Canada (MCI), 2013 FC 314, 226 A.C.W.S. (3d) 1137 at pages 6 and 7: Each case must be determined on its own facts as established by the evidence. This is not a case such as Cervenakova v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship & Immigration), 2012 FC 525 (F.C.) where the Board had failed to properly weigh the documentary evidence, its analysis was vague and there was an insufficient basis for the adequacy conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: Mosley says cases decided on facts; Cervenakova involved vague analysis and insufficient basis for adequacy conclusion.

propositions.text: The Board conducted a forward-looking analysis of the Applicant’s risk of persecution and considered mixed evidence in country condition reports.
propositions.quote: Here the Board conducted a forward-looking analysis of the Applicant’s risk of persecution, and properly considered the mixed evidence contained in the country condition reports.

propositions.text: The Board acknowledged shortcomings in protection for Roma in Slovakia but concluded Applicant failed to rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: The Board acknowledged the shortcomings in the protection available to Roma in Slovakia, but nevertheless concluded that the Applicant had failed to rebut the presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The Board analyzed the Applicant's persecution risk and country evidence, acknowledging protection shortcomings but found Applicant failed to rebut state protection presumption.

propositions.text: The Board's conclusion was open based on evidence provided.
propositions.quote: In my view this conclusion was open to the Board based on the evidence provided.

propositions.text: The Board is not required to refer to every piece of evidence supporting its decision.
propositions.quote: It is trite law that the Board is not required to refer to every piece of evidence that supports its decision.

propositions.text: No indication the Board ignored evidence contradicting its findings; analysis was thorough and well-reasoned.
propositions.quote: There is no indication that the Board ignored evidence that contradicted its findings, and its analysis was thorough and well-reasoned.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board's conclusion was open, not ignoring contradictory evidence, and its analysis thorough and well-reasoned.

propositions.text: The Board’s state protection analysis was reasonable.
propositions.quote: I therefore find that the Board’s state protection analysis was reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Board's state protection analysis reasonable.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review is dismissed.

propositions.text: No certified question for appeal was proposed or arises.
propositions.quote: Neither party proposed a certified question for appeal, and none arises in this case.

propositions.text: Judgment is that the application for judicial review is dismissed and no question is certified for appeal.
propositions.quote: JUDGMENT THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is dismissed. No question is certified for appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the judicial review application and certifies no question for appeal.
